# nish/net/tls/verify

The TLS client's one authentication seam: whether the server a `TlsRecordClient` reached is the one its `serverName` says, decided at `TLS_RECORD_AUTH` and handed to the connection as its verdict.

```ts
import {
  TLS_ALERT_CERTIFICATE_EXPIRED,
  TLS_ALERT_UNKNOWN_CA,
  TLS_VERIFY_MIN_RSA_BITS,
  TlsClientTrust,
  tlsClientAuthenticate,
  tlsClientChain,
  tlsClientSystemTrust,
  tlsClientTrust,
  tlsClientVerdict,
  tlsVerifyCertificateVerify,
} from "nish/net/tls/verify";
```

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="tlsClientAuthenticate" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlsclientauthenticate">

Authenticates `client`'s server, while its interest says `TLS_RECORD_AUTH`: `tlsClientVerdict`, then `client.authenticate(true)` on 0 or `client.reject(alert)` otherwise, which seals the alert.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsClientChain" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlsclientchain">

The chain step: 0 when `chain` (DER, leaf first) leads to a root in `trust` and names `serverName` at `nowMs`, else the alert — `certificate_expired`, `unknown_ca` or `bad_certificate`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsClientSystemTrust" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlsclientsystemtrust">

The trust of the system's roots (`pkiLoadSystemRoots`): what a client trusts unless it is given a store.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsClientTrust" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlsclienttrust">

The trust of `roots`, as `nish/crypto/pki-roots` read them.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsClientVerdict" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlsclientverdict">

The verdict on `tls`'s server at `TLS_CLIENT_STATE_WAIT_AUTH`: 0 when the CertificateVerify verifies under the leaf's key and the chain leads from that leaf to a root in `trust` for the configured server name at `nowMs` (milliseconds since 1970-01-01 UTC), else the alert to refuse with.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsVerifyCertificateVerify" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlsverifycertificateverify">

Whether `signature`, as a CertificateVerify carries it under `scheme`, verifies over `content` under `leaf`'s key.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="TlsClientTrust" icon="phosphor/regular/cube" href="#tlsclienttrust-1">

The roots a client trusts, indexed once and shared by every connection made with them.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>

<scalar-callout type="info">

```ts
const trust: TlsClientTrust = tlsClientSystemTrust();
// when conn.interest() says TLS_RECORD_AUTH:
const alert: i32 = tlsClientAuthenticate(conn, trust, toI64(Date.now()));
```

</scalar-callout>

<scalar-detail title="Two checks, both always made">

The CertificateVerify first: its scheme
must be one this client offered and fit the leaf's key — ECDSA P-256 with
SHA-256 on a P-256 key, ECDSA P-384 with SHA-384 on a P-384 key, RSA-PSS
(rsae, salt as long as the hash) on an RSA key of at least 2048 bits — and
the signature must verify over `TlsClient.verifyContent()` under that key
(RFC 8446 §4.4.3). Then the chain, from the leaf the server sent to a root
in `trust`, for the name the caller dialled. A server with no certificate
or a leaf that does not parse is `bad_certificate`, as is a leaf whose key
is of any other kind (Ed25519, a short RSA modulus); a signature that does
not verify, or a scheme that does not fit the key, is `decrypt_error`.
The signature goes first so a forged CertificateVerify reads as what it is
whatever the chain would have said.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="The chain is nish/crypto/pki's">

`pkiVerifyServer` builds a path from
the leaf to a root of `trust`'s store and checks every certificate on it —
signatures, validity at the instant given, basicConstraints, keyUsage,
serverAuth, name constraints — and that the leaf's subjectAltName names
the host dialled. Its refusal becomes the alert: `certificate_expired` for
a certificate outside its validity, `unknown_ca` when no path reaches a
root of the store, and `bad_certificate` for every other reason. There is
no switch that skips the step and none is to be added: a client that is to
talk to a server it cannot authenticate is given a store holding its
issuing root, never a way around the check (`docs/security/tls.md`, "The
client carrier and verify").

</scalar-detail>

The verdict is the record client's to send: `tlsClientAuthenticate` calls
`authenticate(true)` or `reject(alert)` on it, so the refusal goes out as
a fatal alert under the handshake keys. Written from RFC 8446 §4.2.3 and
§4.4.3, not ported from another implementation.

## tlsClientAuthenticate

Authenticates `client`'s server, while its interest says
`TLS_RECORD_AUTH`: `tlsClientVerdict`, then `client.authenticate(true)` on
0 or `client.reject(alert)` otherwise, which seals the alert. Answers 0
or the alert the connection failed with.

```ts
function tlsClientAuthenticate(
  client: TlsRecordClient,
  trust: TlsClientTrust,
  nowMs: i64,
): i32
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="client" type="TlsRecordClient" required>
</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="trust" type="TlsClientTrust" required>
</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="nowMs" type="i64" required>
</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">
</scalar-field>

## tlsClientVerdict

The verdict on `tls`'s server at `TLS_CLIENT_STATE_WAIT_AUTH`: 0 when the
CertificateVerify verifies under the leaf's key and the chain leads from
that leaf to a root in `trust` for the configured server name at `nowMs`
(milliseconds since 1970-01-01 UTC), else the alert to refuse with.

```ts

  tls: TlsClient,
  trust: TlsClientTrust,
  nowMs: i64,
): i32
```

## tlsVerifyCertificateVerify

Whether `signature`, as a CertificateVerify carries it under `scheme`,
verifies over `content` under `leaf`'s key. `false` for a scheme that
does not fit the key's kind and for every scheme this client does not
offer.

```ts
function tlsVerifyCertificateVerify(
  leaf: X509Certificate,
  scheme: i32,
  content: u8[],
  signature: u8[],
): boolean
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="leaf" type="X509Certificate" required>
</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="scheme" type="i32" required>
</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="content" type="u8[]" required>
</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="signature" type="u8[]" required>
</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">
</scalar-field>

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="45" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_ALERT_CERTIFICATE_EXPIRED: i32`

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="48" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_ALERT_UNKNOWN_CA: i32`

`unknown_ca` (RFC 8446 §6.2): no path from the chain reaches a root the client trusts.
